info.title: Sugrpay platform API
info.description:
Every endpoint of the three APIs: **platform** (sign-in, companies, brands, team, locations, payment-gateway connections), **Sugrpay** (customers, invoices, payments, checks, brand settings, dashboard, Zoho Books, the public payment page) and **HQ** (health only, so far). Each operation says which API serves it and the access it needs.

This document is generated from the code (`pnpm docs:api`), so it always matches what the API does. The guide is [docs/api/README.md](https://github.com/primeshelfspace/platform/blob/main/docs/api/README.md).

## Addresses

In production, `api.sugrpay.com` accepts every path and passes it on to the API that owns it, so **Try it out** works for every endpoint from this page. Locally, each API runs on its own port (platform 4001, Sugrpay 4002, HQ 4003); this page sends each request to the right one.

## Signing in

1. Call `POST /auth/login` with `{ "email", "password" }` (Try it out). It returns `{ token, expiresAt, user }`.
2. Click **Authorize** and paste the `token` under **bearerAuth**. Every signed-in request then carries `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.
3. `POST /auth/logout` ends the session.

Sessions last 12 hours. Five wrong passwords in 15 minutes lock the account for 30 minutes.

## Who may call what

A signed-in request passes, in order: a valid **session** (`401`), the company's **product** subscription for Sugrpay routes (`403`), the role's **permission** (`RESOURCE:ACTION`, shown on each operation) (`403`), and for `/brands/{brandId}/…` a **brand** the user can reach (`403`).

## Conventions

- **Money in responses** is integer minor units in fields ending `Minor` (`totalMinor: 12550` is $125.50). **Money in requests** is a decimal string, as typed (`"unitPrice": "50.00"`). Rates are basis points (`taxRateBp: 875` is 8.75%).
- **IDs** are UUIDs. **Dates** are ISO 8601.
- **Lists** take `?page=1&pageSize=25` (`pageSize` 1–200) and return `{ data, page, pageSize, total }`.
- **Errors** are `{ statusCode, error, message }`; validation errors are `{ message: "validation failed", issues: [{ path, message, code }] }`.
- **Public** routes need no sign-in but are protected another way: the payment-link token, a provider's signature, a signed OAuth `state` or a signed file link.
- **Internal** routes (`/internal/…`) are for the APIs only; nginx refuses them from the internet.

zohoSyncedVersion.description: The last_modified_time Zoho reported for this contact immediately after our own push. Lets ZohoPullService tell our own write echoing back from a genuine edit made in Zoho — without it, a push followed by a pull replaced firstName/lastName with whatever Zoho derived from contact_name, since upsertCustomer sends only contact_name but pullOneCustomer reads first_name/last_name back. Null means "never pushed from here", which correctly reads as "not an echo".

zohoUnsyncedReason.description: Set when a required-field check blocks an outbound Zoho push (FR-ZHO webhook "Outbound"/"mandatory fields"), so the reason is visible on the customer itself, not only in the Sync Dashboard's SyncJob trail. Cleared the moment a push for this customer succeeds.

zohoUnsyncedReason.description: Same purpose as Customer.zohoUnsyncedReason. Payment sync is platform → Zoho only, so this is the only unsynced-reason surface for it.

gatewayReference.description: Uniquely indexed — the mechanism behind NFR-INT-010. A gateway that delivers the same settlement twice cannot create a second payment row.

lastEventAt.description: Gateway's own timestamp for the last event applied. Anything older is discarded, which is what makes out-of-order webhooks safe (NFR-INT-012).

accentColor.description: Brand Settings > Branding > Payment Page — how this brand's hosted payment page arranges itself and colours its actionable elements. Same settings the admin's Payment Page editor previews; this is what actually renders it for a real customer.

customerName.description: Who the invoice is billed to — the "Bill To" block, same identity the admin's own Invoice PDF preview and this brand's issued PDF show.

customerAddress.description: Multi-line (newline-separated), possibly empty when the customer has no billing address on file — same convention as the admin's own formatAddressLines.

invoicePdf.description: Brand Settings > Branding > Invoice PDF — the same settings the admin's Invoice PDF editor previews, applied here so a customer's public invoice page actually reflects the document layout/fields/notes a merchant configured, not a fixed generic summary.

enabledMethods.description: FR-PAY-005 — which methods this brand actually offers. The payment page must only render these; PaymentsService.createIntent enforces the same list server-side regardless of what the client shows.

stripePublishableKey.description: The PLATFORM's publishable key — under Connect the browser loads Stripe.js with this plus the connected account below, rather than with a key belonging to the brand. Null if this deployment has no Stripe configured.

brandThemeColor.description: Always populated (unlike `brandName`, which is null outside All Brands mode to avoid repeating the same name on every row) — the feed's avatar is brand-colored in both modes, same treatment as the By Brand cards.

assignedBrandIds.description: Explicit assignments. Empty for all-brand roles, which do not need them.

products.description: Products the company holds an active subscription to.

productRoles.description: The user's role in each product they may use.

assignedLocationIds.description: Locations (stores, warehouses) explicitly assigned to the user.

product.description: The product serving the current request, once the guard has checked it.

accountId.description: The connected account id (acct_…). Not a secret — it travels in the client-side Elements options and in every webhook payload.

displayName.description: Whatever Stripe knows this business as, for display. Null until the brand finishes Stripe's own onboarding, which can outlast the OAuth redirect.

chargesEnabled.description: False while Stripe is still collecting details from the brand — the account is linked but cannot accept a live charge yet.

brandName.description: Only populated when brandId was omitted from the request.
